notes: TWO CHANGES: the cash-row disclaimer is gone, and instruments inactive across the visible window are hidden. DISCLAIMER REMOVED from the Cash at end of month header, as requested. The header now reads simply 'Cash at end of month — savings + salary account'. The behaviour it described is unchanged: income dated to a later month is still held out of this month's close. INACTIVE INSTRUMENTS HIDDEN. The test is 'zero across every visible month', NOT 'is it closed'. That choice matters in three ways. It needs no lifecycle flag that could drift out of sync with reality, which has been the recurring failure mode in this codebase. It respects the window, so a loan closed in October still appears when viewing August to December, where it was genuinely being paid, and disappears once the window moves to November. And it generalises: closed EMIs, fully redeemed investments and instruments that have not started yet are all covered by one rule. NOTHING DISAPPEARS SILENTLY. A footnote row states how many are hidden and offers to show them, and the choice is session-only so the default on each visit is the uncluttered view. A row vanishing without explanation would be its own form of confusion. SCOPE: EMI and investment rows only. Expense categories are left alone even at zero, since a zero-spend category is a live budget line rather than a dead instrument. ONE CONSEQUENCE, ACCEPTED: an EMI starting in 2028 is hidden while viewing 2026. 'Hidden' means not relevant to this window, not dead. VERIFIED FOR EMIs: viewing Aug-Dec 2026 shows a loan closing in October alongside an active one and hides a loan closed in June, reporting '1 hidden'; moving the window to November hides both closed loans and reports '2 hidden'; the reveal control restores all three. NOT VERIFIED FOR INVESTMENTS, AND SAID SO PLAINLY. The investment filter uses the same rule, applied to the engine's balance series because the engine honours close events directly while the display overlay substitutes reverse-walked figures for past months and can still report a pre-closure balance. It could not be confirmed end to end here: the test harness failed to apply the projection window, so the check ran against the full horizon where a since-closed instrument still held a balance, and the row stayed visible. On real data where a closed instrument reports zero across the window it should hide correctly, but that is reasoning rather than a measurement, and it is worth checking after loading. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard and Decisions-to-chain gaps both remain zero. No page errors.
